newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM seeks ratification of Amoco deal.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM seeks ratification of Amoco deal.

text.p: Latvia's premier will ask parliament to ratify an agreement with U.S. Amoco Corp and Swedish company OPAB to explore for oil in a disputed offshore zone also claimed by neighbouring Lithuania, the Baltic News Service (BNS) said on Thursday.

BNS quoted a senior advisor to Latvian Prime Minister Andris Skele as saying the premier would ask parliament to adopt the agreement, which must take place by October 31 under the terms stipulated last year.

The deal would not come into force until Lithuania and Latvia have agreed on the delimitation of their sea border, but it has sparked bitter protest from Lithuania, which also lays claim to part of the zone in question.
"If the Latvians decide to ratify this agreement, we will recall our ambassador to Latvia," a source in the Lithuanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.

Skele on Monday met his Lithuanian counterpart Mindaugas Stankevicius in a bid to resolve the dispute which has soured relations between the Baltic siblings, but the two premiers failed to reach an agreement.
Five years after quitting the former Soviet Union, Latvia and Lithuania are both keen to exploit domestic energy sources to reduce their dependency on Russia for fuel supplies.
